info.title: DatabaseMax API
info.description:
The DatabaseMax HTTP API. Everything you can do in the dashboard is available here.

**Authentication.** Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer dmx_live_…`. Keys are created in the
dashboard (Settings → API keys) and carry explicit scopes. Browser sessions use an HttpOnly cookie
plus an `X-CSRF-Token` header on state-changing requests.

**Errors** use one shape: `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "details?"}}`.
Every response carries an `X-Request-ID` header.

**Idempotency.** `POST /projects` and `POST /databases` accept an `Idempotency-Key` header; retrying
with the same key returns the original result instead of creating a duplicate.

**Asynchronous provisioning.** `POST /databases` returns `202` immediately; poll
`GET /databases/{id}` (or `/status`) until `status` is `ready`.

Explicit, operator-initiated move (backup → restore on the target, same URL/credentials).
The database is unavailable for writes, then briefly for connections, while it moves.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `agent` marks a machine identity (e.g. an AI agent or automation). Agent keys always need human approval for destructive operations.

requires_approval.title: Requires Approval
requires_approval.description: Require human approval for destructive operations (always on for agent keys)

source_storage_mb.title: Source Storage Mb
source_storage_mb.description: Storage a restore of this backup will allocate

backup_id.title: Backup Id
backup_id.description: Restore this backup; omit to copy the current data

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Defaults to the source database's project

CloneCreate.title: CloneCreate
CloneCreate.description:
Create a new, independent database from a backup (or from the current state of the source,
via a fresh backup). Restores never overwrite an existing database.

DatabaseCreate.title: DatabaseCreate
DatabaseCreate.description:
Only product-level choices. Images, hosts, volumes, networks and privileges are never
accepted from clients (extra fields are rejected).

host_status.title: Host Status
host_status.description: Health of the server the database runs on (the server itself isn't disclosed)

sql.title: Sql
sql.description: Suggested SQL to review and run yourself; never run automatically

interval_seconds.title: Interval Seconds
interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the two samples the rates use

cache_hit_ratio.title: Cache Hit Ratio
cache_hit_ratio.description: Share of block reads served from memory, this interval

position.title: Position
position.description: 1-based character position in the submitted SQL

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: Values in PostgreSQL's text format; null is SQL NULL

row_count.title: Row Count
row_count.description: Rows the statement produced, including rows not returned

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: `read` runs inside a read-only transaction that is always rolled back

confirm_destructive.title: Confirm Destructive
confirm_destructive.description: Required in write mode for DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER, DELETE and UPDATE statements

explain.title: Explain
explain.description: `plan` returns the query plan without running the statement; `analyze` runs it (read-only) and returns actual timings

rolled_back_open_transaction.title: Rolled Back Open Transaction
rolled_back_open_transaction.description: A transaction was left open (BEGIN without COMMIT) and has been rolled back

plan.title: Plan
plan.description: EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) output when `explain` was requested
